title: Honey-Maple Granola with Walnuts, Almonds, Seeds and Raisins
summary: Oats, walnuts, almonds, coconut and seeds are coated with warm maple syrup, honey and oil, baked golden in clusters and mixed with raisins.
equipment: large rimmed baking tray, about 30 x 43 cm

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 160 °C (140 °C fan) with a shelf in the middle. A moderate heat toasts the oats evenly without scorching the nuts.

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.text: Stir the oats, walnuts, almonds, coconut, sesame, sunflower seeds and salt together in the large bowl.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Warm the maple syrup, honey and oil in the small saucepan, whisking, until runny and just warm. Pour over the dry mixture and stir until every flake is coated. Warm syrup spreads more evenly.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Tip onto the baking tray, spread evenly and press down lightly so the mixture bakes into clusters.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for 15-20 minutes, stirring and re-spreading after 8 and 15 minutes, until light golden. Watch the final minutes, as nuts burn quickly.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Tip onto the second tray to stop the cooking, stir in the raisins, press flat and leave to cool completely on the rack, about 30 minutes. It crisps as it cools, so don't judge it while warm. Break into clusters.

steps.title: Store and serve
steps.text: Keep in the airtight jar. Serve 60 g with yoghurt or milk.

tips: Taking it out too late is the commonest mistake; it should be light golden, as it keeps colouring on the hot tray.
Add the raisins after baking, or they turn hard and bitter.
For bigger clusters, stir less and press the mixture down firmly.
Let it cool completely before storing, or it softens.
storage: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 weeks. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
